scope: Complete standalone candidate with inherited mock DOM; real ROM/frame lifecycle, pointer controls and controller settings, fullscreen success/denial/races. No real layout, native user activation, physical controller, audio or browser/device acceptance.

results.name: Play UI startup preserves intrinsic canvas size and accurately labels default touch visibility
Enter and exit retain the same canvas, ROM, framebuffer, running state and editor project
Expanded view hides editor siblings from focus/assistive access and restores their prior values
Protected Save As exits expanded view, restores dialog access and preserves its focused field
Ctrl and Command Save reach the actual protected export handler from focused player controls
Real pointer controls combine D-pad movement with A and B and release individual fingers
Lost capture, leaving D-pad bounds and hiding controls never leave a NES button held
Pause/resume invalidates old touch-pointer ownership until a new pointerdown
Touch buttons are keyboard accessible without leaking Enter into NES Start
Controller settings pause playback, block input, and leave resumption explicit
Controller mapper waits for release and captures a button or signed axis with input blocked
Player status reflects controller selection, neutralization and disconnect
Fullscreen unsupported and rejected requests retain usable expanded play without resetting state
Successful container fullscreen includes the original canvas and cleans up on exit
A late rejected fullscreen request cannot steal focus after Exit
A late successful fullscreen request is dismissed, and concurrent requests do not overlap
Changing editor tab exits expanded view, closes settings and releases touch input
Play settings retain native selector keyboard behavior while containing Escape
